idiom_name: delegated property (by) whose getValue/setValue checks on every access
implementation_notes: Kotlin's property delegation is a natural mediation point: 'val x by Guarded(delegate)' routes every read through the delegate's getValue (and every write through setValue), so the check is part of the access instead of a separate call. The classic wrapper collapses into that delegate plus private or internal visibility for the backing object, and a private-set property whose setter validates. Two forms must be avoided: by lazy and any memoizing delegate perform the check once and then return a remembered result, which is exactly the stale-decision failure the principle warns about - the honest form re-evaluates in getValue. On the JVM reflection (setAccessible) still reaches private members, so this is in-process mediation for code you trust, not a boundary against arbitrary code.
pitfalls: by lazy (and any caching delegate) makes the mediation one-shot: the first read is checked, later reads are not - a delegated property is only complete if getValue re-evaluates.
internal visibility is module-scoped and compile-time only; another module can still reach the JVM classes through reflection, and internal members are public in the bytecode.

A delegated property is readable by anyone holding the owner, so the owner must not expose the backing reference through a getter, a data-class copy or a constructor parameter that is also stored publicly.
A delegate that captures thisRef can keep the owner alive; shared or pooled delegates turn that into a lifetime leak.
